model.name: Model
model.definition: A simplified representation of some part of reality, chosen to make it graspable and to predict it.

representation.name: Representation
representation.definition: Something that stands in for a set of experiences or objects so they can be reasoned about as one thing.

clustering.name: Clustering
clustering.definition: Grouping unlabeled data points so that points in the same group are more similar to each other than to points in other groups.

abstraction.name: Abstraction
abstraction.definition: Deliberately ignoring details so that many different things can be treated as one; every model is a choice of what to ignore.

extrapolation.name: Extrapolation
extrapolation.definition: Using a pattern compressed from past observations to predict cases beyond those observations.

induction.name: Induction
induction.definition: Inferring a general rule from repeated specific observations, such as concluding the sun will rise because it always has.

domain-of-validity.name: Domain of validity
domain-of-validity.definition: The range of conditions under which a model gives useful predictions, beyond which it breaks down.

falsification.name: Falsification
falsification.definition: Testing a model by actively trying to prove it wrong, since a model can never be proven right.

model-refinement.name: Model refinement
model-refinement.definition: Replacing a working model with a deeper one that explains it and extends further, as kinetic theory did for temperature.

function-approximation.name: Function approximation
function-approximation.definition: Finding a function F that maps inputs x to outputs y from examples, the common shape of most machine learning tasks.

supervised-learning.name: Supervised learning
supervised-learning.definition: Learning a mapping from inputs to outputs using examples where the correct output is given.

previewed_on.title: What Could X and Y Be?

unsupervised-learning.name: Unsupervised learning
unsupervised-learning.definition: Finding structure in data that comes without labels, such as clusters or low-dimensional directions.

program.name: Program
program.definition: A precise sequence of instructions that a computer follows exactly, with no common sense to fill gaps.

programming-language.name: Programming language
programming-language.definition: A formal language, like Python, in which every statement has exactly one meaning, used to write programs.

arithmetic-operator.name: Arithmetic operator
arithmetic-operator.definition: A symbol such as +, /, ** or % that computes a number from other numbers in code.

variable.name: Variable
variable.definition: A name attached to a value in a program so it can be referred to and reused.

assignment.name: Assignment
assignment.definition: The action written with = in code: compute the right-hand side, then attach the name on the left to the result.

data-type.name: Data type
data-type.definition: The kind of a value (number, text, boolean) that determines what operations on it mean.

list.name: List
list.definition: An ordered collection of values in a program, accessed by position.

indexing.name: Indexing
indexing.definition: Retrieving an element of a sequence by its position, counting from zero in Python.

conditional.name: Conditional
conditional.definition: An if/else statement that runs different code depending on whether a condition is true.

loop.name: Loop
loop.definition: A statement that repeats a block of code for each item or until a stopping rule is met.

execution-trace.name: Execution trace
execution-trace.definition: Following a program line by line while tracking what value each name holds, to see what the computer actually does.

function.name: Function
function.definition: A named, reusable rule that takes inputs and returns an output, both in mathematics and as a recipe in code.

dictionary.name: Dictionary
dictionary.definition: A container that maps keys to values, so a value is found by its key rather than by its position.

debugging.name: Debugging
debugging.definition: Finding and fixing errors in a program, starting by reading what the error message says.

symbolic-ai.title: Overwhelming Optimism
symbolic-ai.name: Symbolic AI
symbolic-ai.definition: The early approach to artificial intelligence that hand-codes rules and searches over symbols, rather than learning from data.

machine-learning.title: Why the Recent Hype?
machine-learning.name: Machine learning
machine-learning.definition: Building systems that learn rules or patterns from data instead of having them programmed by hand.

moores-law.title: Faster Computers
moores-law.name: Moore's law
moores-law.definition: The observation that the number of transistors on a chip roughly doubles every two years.

compute-scaling.title: And What That Bought
compute-scaling.name: Compute scaling
compute-scaling.definition: The growth by many orders of magnitude of the computation used to train AI systems, a main driver of recent progress.

log-scale.title: Or Just Ask For the Plot
log-scale.name: Log scale
log-scale.definition: A plot axis where equal distances mean equal ratios, used when values span many orders of magnitude.

curve-fitting.title: A Lot of It Is Curve Fitting
curve-fitting.name: Curve fitting
curve-fitting.definition: Choosing a function whose curve passes close to a set of data points.

graph.title: Sometimes It Is About Graphs
graph.name: Graph
graph.definition: A set of nodes connected by edges, used to represent relationships such as social networks, maps or molecules.

data-representation.title: What are* data?
data-representation.name: Data representation
data-representation.definition: The way something recorded from the world, like sound, images or text, is turned into numbers a machine can process.

tabular-data.title: Stocks
tabular-data.name: Tabular data
tabular-data.definition: Data arranged as a table, where each row is an example and each column is a measured quantity.

time-series.title: Stocks
time-series.name: Time series
time-series.definition: A sequence of measurements indexed by time, such as a stock price recorded each day.

audio-signal.title: Audio
audio-signal.name: Audio signal
audio-signal.definition: Sound recorded as an array of air-pressure samples taken many thousands of times per second.

spectrogram.title: From a Wave to a Picture
spectrogram.name: Spectrogram
spectrogram.definition: A picture of a sound showing how much energy each frequency has over time, built from short-time Fourier transforms.

fourier-transform.title: From a Wave to a Picture
fourier-transform.name: Fourier transform
fourier-transform.definition: A transformation that rewrites a signal as a sum of sinusoids, revealing which frequencies it contains.

image-representation.title: Images
image-representation.name: Image representation
image-representation.definition: An image stored as a grid of pixel values, of shape height by width by number of channels.

color-channel.title: Colour Is Three Matrices
color-channel.name: Color channel
color-channel.definition: One of the red, green or blue grids of intensities that together make up a colour image.

tensor.title: Video
tensor.name: Tensor
tensor.definition: A multi-dimensional array of numbers, such as a video of shape time by height by width by channels.

word-embedding.title: Text
word-embedding.name: Word embedding
word-embedding.definition: A dense vector for each word, learned so that directions and distances between vectors carry meaning.

adjacency-matrix.title: Graph Representation
adjacency-matrix.name: Adjacency matrix
adjacency-matrix.definition: A matrix whose entry (i, j) is 1 when node i connects to node j, representing a graph as numbers.

modeling-learning-inference.title: The Three Pillars of Artificial Intelligence
modeling-learning-inference.name: Modeling, learning, inference
modeling-learning-inference.definition: The three pillars of AI: build a simplified model, estimate its parameters from data, then use it to answer questions.

classification.title: Classification, Regression, Structured Prediction
classification.name: Classification
classification.definition: Predicting a discrete label, such as fraud or not fraud, from an input.

regression.title: Classification, Regression, Structured Prediction
regression.name: Regression
regression.definition: Predicting a continuous numerical value, such as a house price, from an input.

structured-prediction.title: Classification, Regression, Structured Prediction
structured-prediction.name: Structured prediction
structured-prediction.definition: Predicting an output with internal structure, such as a sentence or a parse tree, rather than a single label or number.

histogram.title: Histogram and Probability Density Function
histogram.name: Histogram
histogram.definition: A bar chart of how many data samples fall into each range of values.

probability-density-function.title: Histogram and Probability Density Function
probability-density-function.name: Probability density function
probability-density-function.definition: A curve describing how likely a continuous variable is to take values near each point; a model of the data, unlike the histogram.

notation-and-code.title: Every Idea, Written Twice
notation-and-code.name: Notation and code
notation-and-code.definition: Every mathematical idea in the course is written two ways, as compact notation and as runnable code, and each translates directly into the other.

iteration.title: The loop that predicts the future
iteration.name: Iteration
iteration.definition: Repeating one update step in a loop, so that a model like next year's population from this year's steps forward through time.

vectors.title: Vectors
vectors.name: Vectors
vectors.definition: An ordered list of numbers, pictured as an arrow with direction and length; in machine learning one example, one row of data, is a vector.

inner-product.title: Vector Operations
inner-product.name: Inner product
inner-product.definition: The sum of elementwise products of two vectors, also called the dot product; the single most common operation in machine learning.

norm.title: How Long, How Far, How Similar
norm.name: Norm
norm.definition: A measure of a vector's length, such as the L2 (Euclidean), L1 (sum of absolute values), or max norm; distances between examples are norms of differences.

cosine-similarity.title: How Long, How Far, How Similar
cosine-similarity.name: Cosine similarity
cosine-similarity.definition: The cosine of the angle between two vectors, their dot product divided by both lengths, measuring how similar their directions are regardless of size.

matrix.title: Matrices
matrix.name: Matrix
matrix.definition: A rectangular array of numbers with rows and columns; it can hold a whole dataset or act as a linear transformation of vectors.

matrix-product.title: Matrices in NumPy
matrix-product.name: Matrix multiplication
matrix-product.definition: Combining two matrices so each output entry is a row-by-column dot product; in NumPy it is A @ B, not the elementwise A * B.

linear-transformation.title: A matrix is a machine that moves space
linear-transformation.name: Linear transformation
linear-transformation.definition: A map that moves space while keeping lines straight and the origin fixed; a matrix's columns record where the basis vectors land.

determinant.title: A matrix is a machine that moves space
determinant.name: Determinant
determinant.definition: The factor by which a matrix scales area or volume; a determinant of zero means the matrix flattens space and cannot be inverted.

eigenvector.title: A matrix is a machine that moves space
eigenvector.name: Eigenvector
eigenvector.definition: A direction that a matrix only stretches or shrinks without turning; the stretch factor is its eigenvalue.

composition.title: Two machines in a row are one machine
composition.name: Composition of transformations
composition.definition: Applying one linear transformation after another, which equals multiplying their matrices; order matters, so RS generally differs from SR.

column-space.title: Two Ways to Read Ax
column-space.name: Column space
column-space.definition: The set of all outputs Ax, read as weighted sums of the columns of A, where x supplies the weights.

span.title: Span, Independence, Rank
span.name: Span
span.definition: Everything you can build from a set of vectors by scaling and adding them together.

rank.title: Span, Independence, Rank
rank.name: Rank
rank.definition: The number of linearly independent columns of a matrix, which is the dimension of the space its outputs can reach.

inverse.title: Inverse, Determinant, and When Things Break
inverse.name: Matrix inverse
inverse.definition: The matrix that undoes A, so multiplying them gives the identity; it solves the linear system Ax = b when it exists.

condition-number.title: When the Inverse Quietly Lies
condition-number.name: Condition number
condition-number.definition: A measure of how much a matrix amplifies small errors when inverted; nearly duplicate columns make it huge and the solution unreliable.

derivative.title: A derivative is what a curve looks like up close
derivative.name: Derivative
derivative.definition: The slope of a curve at a point, what the curve looks like up close: how fast the output changes as the input nudges.

integral.title: A rate and its total
integral.name: Integral
integral.definition: The accumulated total of a rate, the area under its curve; integration and differentiation undo each other.

gradient.title: The Calculus You Actually Need
gradient.name: Gradient
gradient.definition: The vector of partial derivatives of a function with respect to each parameter, pointing in the direction of steepest increase.

normal-equations.title: The One Gradient You Will Use All Semester
normal-equations.name: Normal equations
normal-equations.definition: The linear system obtained by setting the least-squares gradient to zero, whose solution gives the best-fit parameters in closed form.

projection.title: Least Squares Is a Projection
projection.name: Projection
projection.definition: The closest point to a vector within a subspace; least squares projects the targets onto the space spanned by the feature columns.

chain-rule.title: The chain rule, as a picture
chain-rule.name: Chain rule
chain-rule.definition: The rule that the derivative of a composition is the product of the derivatives of its parts, which is how networks compute gradients.

backpropagation.title: The chain rule, as a picture
backpropagation.name: Backpropagation
backpropagation.definition: Computing all gradients of a network efficiently by applying the chain rule backward from the loss through each operation.

aliasing.title: A variable is a label, not a box
aliasing.name: Variable aliasing
aliasing.definition: A Python variable is a label on an object, not a box, so two names can share one object and a change through either shows in both.

broadcasting.title: Broadcasting, and the Bug It Causes
broadcasting.name: Broadcasting
broadcasting.definition: NumPy's rule for combining arrays of different shapes by stretching size-one dimensions, a convenience that also causes silent shape bugs.

vectorization.title: Avoid Loops if You Can! Vectorize.
vectorization.name: Vectorization
vectorization.definition: Replacing explicit Python loops with whole-array operations, which run in optimized compiled code and are often hundreds of times faster.

dataframe.title: Reading and Exploring Data
dataframe.name: DataFrame
dataframe.definition: A pandas table of labeled columns used to read, inspect, summarize, and clean a dataset before turning it into numeric arrays.

previewed_on.title: Or Just Ask For the Plot

design-matrix.title: The Design Matrix
design-matrix.name: Design matrix
design-matrix.definition: The data matrix with one row per example and one column per feature, with the target held in a separate vector.

correlation.title: Statistics Is Linear Algebra
correlation.name: Correlation
correlation.definition: A number between minus one and one measuring how linearly two variables move together, the dot product of their standardized columns divided by their count.

missing-variable.title: The Same Data, Two Answers
missing-variable.name: Missing variable (Simpson's paradox)
missing-variable.definition: A trend in pooled data can reverse within groups when a hidden variable, such as species, drives both measurements.

dataset.title: Data
dataset.name: Dataset
dataset.definition: A table of examples and measurements that you can visualize, summarize, clean, and use to make predictions.

previewed_on.title: 1. What Could ML Do for X?

feature.title: Inputs and Outputs
feature.name: Feature
feature.definition: An input variable given to the model, such as a house's size, bedrooms, or age.

target.title: Inputs and Outputs
target.name: Target
target.definition: The output variable the model is trying to predict, also called the label, such as a house's price.

training-example.title: Inputs and Outputs
training-example.name: Training example
training-example.definition: One input and output pair from the data, indexed by i, used to fit the model.

hypothesis.title: The Hypothesis
hypothesis.name: Hypothesis
hypothesis.definition: The function a learning algorithm chooses to map inputs to predicted outputs.

parameters.title: The Hypothesis
parameters.name: Parameters
parameters.definition: The numbers, often called theta, that select one specific function from within the chosen model class and are adjusted by training.

model-class.title: The Hypothesis
model-class.name: Model class
model-class.definition: The family of candidate functions a learner searches over, such as linear, polynomial, or neural network models.

linear-model.title: The Linear Hypothesis
linear-model.name: Linear model
linear-model.definition: A prediction that is a weighted sum of the features plus an intercept, written as a single inner product of parameters and inputs.

intercept.title: The Linear Hypothesis
intercept.name: Intercept
intercept.definition: The constant term of a linear model, handled by adding a feature that is always one; it is the prediction when all features are zero.

residual.title: The Cost Function
residual.name: Residual
residual.definition: The difference between a model's prediction and the actual target for one example.

cost-function.title: The Cost Function
cost-function.name: Cost function
cost-function.definition: A single number measuring how badly the model fits the data, such as half the sum of squared residuals, which training tries to minimize.

loss-landscape.title: The Loss Landscape
loss-landscape.name: Loss landscape
loss-landscape.definition: The surface formed by the cost at every possible parameter setting; its lowest point is the best fit.

gradient-descent.title: Gradient Descent
gradient-descent.name: Gradient descent
gradient-descent.definition: An optimization method that repeatedly steps the parameters a small amount opposite the gradient, walking downhill on the cost.

previewed_on.title: The One Gradient You Will Use All Semester

learning-rate.title: Gradient Descent
learning-rate.name: Learning rate
learning-rate.definition: The step size in gradient descent; too small is slow, too large overshoots and can diverge.

lms-rule.title: Computing the Gradient
lms-rule.name: LMS update rule
lms-rule.definition: The least-mean-squares gradient step for linear regression, which moves each parameter in proportion to the prediction error times its feature.

sgd.title: Watch It Learn
sgd.name: Stochastic gradient descent
sgd.definition: Gradient descent that updates the parameters using one randomly chosen example (or small batch) per step, giving a faster but noisier path.

centering.title: Why we measure from the average house
centering.name: Centering features
centering.definition: Subtracting a feature's mean so the intercept describes a typical example, which decouples slope and intercept and speeds up gradient descent.

multiple-regression.title: What is a bedroom worth?
multiple-regression.name: Multiple regression
multiple-regression.definition: Linear regression with several features at once, where each coefficient's value depends on which other features are included.

holding-fixed.title: θj answers one question at a time
holding-fixed.name: Holding other variables fixed
holding-fixed.definition: A regression coefficient is the change in prediction per unit of its feature with every other feature held fixed, so it depends on the company it keeps.

gaussian-noise.title: Why Least Squares? A Probabilistic View
gaussian-noise.name: Gaussian noise model
gaussian-noise.definition: The assumption that each target equals the model's prediction plus independent, normally distributed noise with mean zero.

likelihood.title: The Likelihood of the Data
likelihood.name: Likelihood
likelihood.definition: The probability of the observed data viewed as a function of the parameters; for independent examples it is a product over them.

maximum-likelihood.title: Least Squares Is Maximum Likelihood
maximum-likelihood.name: Maximum likelihood estimation
maximum-likelihood.definition: Choosing parameters that make the observed data most probable; with Gaussian noise this is exactly least squares.

outlier.title: Five strange sales
outlier.name: Outlier
outlier.definition: An unusual data point far from the pattern; squared error lets it pull the fit strongly toward itself.

l1-loss.title: Five strange sales
l1-loss.name: Absolute error (L1 loss)
l1-loss.definition: A cost that sums absolute residuals instead of squared ones, which corresponds to Laplacian noise and is less sensitive to outliers.

k-nearest-neighbours.title: Given a new input, what’s the output?
k-nearest-neighbours.name: k-nearest neighbours
k-nearest-neighbours.definition: Predicting the output for a new input by averaging the outputs of the k training examples closest to it.

hypothesis-choice.title: How do you choose the hypothesis?
hypothesis-choice.name: Choosing the hypothesis
hypothesis-choice.definition: The same data admits many fitting functions, so deciding which family of functions to use is a central modeling choice.

feature-map.title: A Feature Built in 1885
feature-map.name: Feature map
feature-map.definition: A transformation that builds new features from raw inputs, such as Galton's mid-parent height or polynomial powers of x, before fitting a model.

regression-to-the-mean.title: Where the Word Comes From
regression-to-the-mean.name: Regression to the mean
regression-to-the-mean.definition: Galton's finding that children of unusually tall or short parents tend to be closer to average, which gave regression its name.

r-squared.title: A Fifth of the Variance, and a Whole Discipline
r-squared.name: R squared
r-squared.definition: The fraction of the target's variance explained by a fit: one minus residual variation over total variation.

overfitting.title: How to choose φ(x)? How to optimize over φ(x)
overfitting.name: Overfitting
overfitting.definition: When a model is too flexible and fits noise in the training data, giving low training error but poor performance on new data (high variance).

previewed_on.title: Why Not Interpolate All the Points?

underfitting.title: How to choose φ(x)? How to optimize over φ(x)
underfitting.name: Underfitting
underfitting.definition: When a model is too simple to capture the real pattern, giving high error even on the training data (high bias).

generalization.title: How can we tell if φ(·) is good?
generalization.name: Generalization
generalization.definition: A model's ability to perform well on new, unseen data, which is the real goal of machine learning.

previewed_on.title: Why Not Interpolate All the Points?

test-set.title: How can we tell if φ(·) is good?
test-set.name: Test set
test-set.definition: Data held out from training and used once at the end to estimate how well the model generalizes.

bias-variance.title: Variance Bias Trade-off
bias-variance.name: Bias-variance trade-off
bias-variance.definition: As model complexity grows, error from too-simple assumptions (bias) falls while error from sensitivity to the particular data (variance) rises.

hyperparameter.title: Other Hyperparameters
hyperparameter.name: Hyperparameter
hyperparameter.definition: A setting chosen outside the training loop, such as the number of epochs, the step size, or the feature map.

validation-set.title: Optimize over φ and other hyperparameters
validation-set.name: Validation set
validation-set.definition: Held-out data used during development to compare models and tune hyperparameters, kept separate from the final test set.

cross-validation.title: Cross validation: every house takes a turn being new
cross-validation.name: Cross-validation
cross-validation.definition: Splitting data into folds and letting each fold take a turn as the validation set, averaging the results for a more reliable estimate.

regularization.title: Regularization
regularization.name: Regularization
regularization.definition: Adding a penalty on parameter size to the cost, weighted by lambda, to shrink the hypothesis class and reduce overfitting.

l2-regularization.title: L2 regularization
l2-regularization.name: L2 regularization
l2-regularization.definition: A penalty on the squared size of the parameters (ridge) that shrinks all coefficients smoothly toward zero.

l1-regularization.title: L1 regularization
l1-regularization.name: L1 regularization
l1-regularization.definition: A penalty on the sum of absolute parameter values (lasso) that tends to drive some coefficients exactly to zero.

sigmoid.title: What if y is a label?
sigmoid.name: Sigmoid
sigmoid.definition: The logistic function 1/(1+e^-z), which squashes any real score into a probability between 0 and 1.

previewed_on.title: What if y is a label?

logistic-regression.title: What if y is a label?
logistic-regression.name: Logistic regression
logistic-regression.definition: A classifier that passes a linear score through the sigmoid function to output the probability that the label is one.

negative-log-likelihood.title: Log, Then Average
negative-log-likelihood.name: Negative log-likelihood
negative-log-likelihood.definition: The negative logarithm of the likelihood, averaged over examples, used as a loss to minimise.

convexity.title: Binary Cross-Entropy
convexity.name: Convexity
convexity.definition: A property of a function shaped like a bowl, so that any local minimum is the global minimum.

cross-entropy.title: Binary Cross-Entropy
cross-entropy.name: Cross-entropy loss
cross-entropy.definition: The loss for predicted probabilities that is near zero when confident and right and grows without bound when confident and wrong.

decision-boundary.title: The Geometry of the Boundary
decision-boundary.name: Decision boundary
decision-boundary.definition: The surface in input space where a classifier switches its prediction from one class to another.

margin.title: The Margin
margin.name: Margin
margin.definition: The signed distance of a point from the decision boundary, positive when it is classified correctly.

confusion-matrix.title: Step 4: Test. But Accuracy of What?
confusion-matrix.name: Confusion matrix
confusion-matrix.definition: A table counting true positives, false positives, false negatives and true negatives of a classifier.

precision-and-recall.title: Step 4: Test. But Accuracy of What?
precision-and-recall.name: Precision and recall
precision-and-recall.definition: Precision is the fraction of flagged cases that are real; recall is the fraction of real cases that were flagged.

accuracy.title: Step 4: Test. But Accuracy of What?
accuracy.name: Accuracy
accuracy.definition: The fraction of all predictions that are correct, which can mislead when classes are imbalanced.

f1-score.title: The Same Four Numbers on One Screening
f1-score.name: F1 score
f1-score.definition: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, a single number that is low if either one is low.

class-imbalance.title: When Accuracy Lies: Imbalanced Data
class-imbalance.name: Class imbalance
class-imbalance.definition: When one class is much rarer than the others, so that always predicting the majority class looks accurate.

classification-threshold.title: When Accuracy Lies: Imbalanced Data
classification-threshold.name: Classification threshold
classification-threshold.definition: The probability cutoff above which a classifier predicts the positive class, chosen after training to trade precision against recall.

multiclass-classification.title: Higher dimensional outputs
multiclass-classification.name: Multiclass classification
multiclass-classification.definition: Classification where the label can take one of more than two values.

one-vs-all.title: How to turn scores into probabilities?Note: this slide explains the intuition. Softmax regression is not exactly equivalent to a combination of one-vs-all classifiers.
one-vs-all.name: One-vs-all
one-vs-all.definition: Handling many classes by training one binary classifier per class against all the others.

softmax.title: How to turn scores into probabilities?
softmax.name: Softmax
softmax.definition: A function that turns a vector of scores into probabilities by exponentiating and normalising them.

softmax-regression.title: How to turn scores into probabilities?
softmax-regression.name: Softmax regression
softmax-regression.definition: The generalisation of logistic regression to many classes, with one linear score per class passed through softmax.

logit.title: How do you train?
logit.name: Logit
logit.definition: The raw score of a class before it is turned into a probability by a sigmoid or softmax.

bernoulli.title: The Bernoulli Distribution
bernoulli.name: Bernoulli distribution
bernoulli.definition: The distribution of a single yes or no outcome, equal to one with probability p and zero with probability one minus p.

exponential-family.title: The Exponential Family
exponential-family.name: Exponential family
exponential-family.definition: A broad class of distributions, including Gaussian, Bernoulli, and Poisson, sharing one form that yields the same learning update rule.

natural-parameter.title: The Exponential Family
natural-parameter.name: Natural parameter
natural-parameter.definition: The parameter eta of an exponential-family distribution that multiplies the outcome inside the exponential; in a GLM it equals the linear score of the inputs.

log-partition-function.title: The Exponential Family
log-partition-function.name: Log partition function
log-partition-function.definition: The term in an exponential-family distribution that normalizes probabilities to sum to one; its derivatives give the mean and variance.

poisson-distribution.title: Example 3: Poisson Becomes Log-Linear Regression
poisson-distribution.name: Poisson distribution
poisson-distribution.definition: The distribution of the number of independent events in a fixed window, such as earthquakes in a decade, governed by an average rate.

poisson-regression.title: How many earthquakes of each size?
poisson-regression.name: Poisson regression
poisson-regression.definition: A generalized linear model for count data where the logarithm of the expected count is linear in the features.

generalized-linear-model.title: Same loop, three models
generalized-linear-model.name: Generalized linear model
generalized-linear-model.definition: A model that passes a linear score of the inputs through a response function matched to an exponential-family output, with the same training loop.

link-function.title: Terminology
link-function.name: Link function
link-function.definition: The function connecting a GLM's expected output to its linear score; its inverse, the response function, turns the score into a prediction.

one-hot.title: Language: One-Hot Word Representation
one-hot.name: One-hot encoding
one-hot.definition: Representing each item of a fixed vocabulary as a vector of zeros with a single one in its own position.

bag-of-words.title: Bag of Words
bag-of-words.name: Bag of words
bag-of-words.definition: Representing a document by which vocabulary words it contains, ignoring their order.

class-conditional.title: What Are the Relevant Probabilities?
class-conditional.name: Class-conditional probability
class-conditional.definition: The probability of a feature given the class label, such as how often the word free appears in spam.

naive-bayes-assumption.title: The Naive Assumption
naive-bayes-assumption.name: Naive Bayes assumption
naive-bayes-assumption.definition: The simplifying assumption that features are conditionally independent given the label, so a message's probability is a product over its words.

bayes-rule.title: Bayes Rule Turns It Around
bayes-rule.name: Bayes' rule
bayes-rule.definition: A formula that reverses conditional probabilities, getting the probability of a label given the data from the probability of the data given the label and the prior.

prior.title: Bayes Rule Turns It Around
prior.name: Prior
prior.definition: The probability of a class before seeing any features, such as how common spam is overall.

naive-bayes.title: For a Given Dataset
naive-bayes.name: Naive Bayes classifier
naive-bayes.definition: A classifier that estimates class priors and per-feature class-conditional probabilities by counting, then combines them with Bayes' rule.

laplace-smoothing.title: The word it never saw
laplace-smoothing.name: Laplace smoothing
laplace-smoothing.definition: Adding a small count to every word and class so that an unseen word does not get probability zero and wipe out the whole product.

event-model.title: Two ways to generate an email
event-model.name: Event model
event-model.definition: The assumed story of how a message is generated, either a coin flip per vocabulary word (multivariate Bernoulli) or words drawn one at a time (multinomial).

generative-model.title: Generative and Discriminative
generative-model.name: Generative model
generative-model.definition: A model that learns how each class's data is distributed, plus the class priors, then classifies with Bayes' rule and can generate new examples.

discriminative-model.title: Generative and Discriminative
discriminative-model.name: Discriminative model
discriminative-model.definition: A model that learns the probability of the label given the input directly, drawing the decision boundary without modeling the inputs.

multivariate-gaussian.title: A Gaussian in two dimensions
multivariate-gaussian.name: Multivariate Gaussian
multivariate-gaussian.definition: The bell-shaped distribution over vectors, described by a mean vector and a covariance matrix that sets its spreads and correlations.

covariance.title: A Gaussian in two dimensions
covariance.name: Covariance matrix
covariance.definition: A matrix whose diagonal holds each variable's variance and whose off-diagonal entries measure how pairs of variables vary together.

gda.title: Gaussian discriminant analysis, on penguins
gda.name: Gaussian discriminant analysis
gda.definition: A generative classifier that models each class's features as a multivariate Gaussian and classifies new points using Bayes' rule.

language-model.title: Auto-Regressive Language Models
language-model.name: Language model
language-model.definition: A model that assigns probabilities to text by predicting each next word from the words before it.

previewed_on.title: A Language Model in One Line

n-gram.title: Auto-Regressive Language Models
n-gram.name: n-gram model
n-gram.definition: A language model that predicts the next word from only the previous few words, estimated by counting word sequences.

threshold-unit.title: The McCulloch-Pitts neuron (1943)
threshold-unit.name: Threshold unit (McCulloch-Pitts neuron)
threshold-unit.definition: An artificial neuron that outputs one when a weighted sum of its inputs reaches a threshold and zero otherwise, enough to build logic gates.

layer.title: Two Outputs Make a Matrix
layer.name: Layer
layer.definition: A set of units computed together, where each output is a weighted sum of all inputs, so the whole layer is one matrix times the input vector.

activation-function.title: The Nonlinear Predictor
activation-function.name: Activation function
activation-function.definition: A nonlinear function applied after each linear step in a network; without it, stacked layers collapse into a single linear map.

relu.title: The Activation Menu
relu.name: ReLU
relu.definition: The rectified linear unit activation, which outputs its input when positive and zero otherwise.

neural-network.title: Neural Network
neural-network.name: Neural network
neural-network.definition: A model built by alternating linear maps and nonlinear activations, learning its own features in hidden layers.

previewed_on.title: What if the boundary needs to curve?
Why Complex Systems Matter for ML

hidden-layer.title: Neural Network
hidden-layer.name: Hidden layer
hidden-layer.definition: An intermediate layer between input and output whose activations are features the network learns for itself.

deep-network.title: Going deep
deep-network.name: Deep network
deep-network.definition: A neural network with many stacked hidden layers, each building features from the layer before it.

universal-approximation.title: How Expressive Is One Hidden Layer?
universal-approximation.name: Universal approximation
universal-approximation.definition: The theorem that one hidden layer with enough neurons and a non-polynomial activation can approximate any continuous function on a bounded domain.

convolution.title: Convolutional networks
convolution.name: Convolution
convolution.definition: Sliding one small set of shared weights (a kernel) across an image so the same pattern is detected wherever it appears.

autoencoder.title: Auto-encoders
autoencoder.name: Autoencoder
autoencoder.definition: A network trained to reproduce its input through a narrow bottleneck, learning a compressed representation with an encoder and decoder.

recurrent-network.title: Recurrent networks
recurrent-network.name: Recurrent neural network
recurrent-network.definition: A network that processes sequences step by step, carrying a hidden state that acts as memory from one step to the next.

computation-graph.title: Computation graphs
computation-graph.name: Computation graph
computation-graph.definition: A representation of a formula as a graph of small operations, each knowing its local derivatives, which makes automatic backpropagation possible.

superposition.title: Before Computers
superposition.name: Superposition
superposition.definition: In a linear system, the response to a sum of inputs is the sum of the responses, so a problem can be split into parts and the solutions added.

nonlinearity.title: The Great Limitation
nonlinearity.name: Nonlinearity
nonlinearity.definition: A system is nonlinear when its response is not proportional to its input, so superposition fails and closed-form solutions are usually out of reach.

numerical-simulation.title: Computers Change Everything
numerical-simulation.name: Numerical simulation
numerical-simulation.definition: Computing an approximate solution of a model, typically a differential equation, step by step on a computer instead of solving it on paper.

scientific-modeling-cycle.title: The Modern Scientific Process
scientific-modeling-cycle.name: Scientific modeling cycle
scientific-modeling-cycle.definition: The loop of deriving equations, building a solver, simulating, comparing predictions with observations, and refining the model.

empirical-law.title: Classical Empirical Laws
empirical-law.name: Empirical law
empirical-law.definition: A law found by measuring how a controlled input changes an output, usually a simple proportionality whose constant gets a physical meaning, like Hooke's or Ohm's law.

least-squares.title: The Birth of Curve Fitting
least-squares.name: Least squares
least-squares.definition: Fitting a model by choosing parameters that minimise the sum of squared differences between predictions and data, developed by Legendre and Gauss.

compression-reconstruction.title: From the World to a Model, and Back
compression-reconstruction.name: Compression and reconstruction
compression-reconstruction.definition: Learning compresses many observations into a compact model, and inference reconstructs high-dimensional predictions from that model.

equation-discovery.title: The Same Three Pillars, for a Field
equation-discovery.name: Equation discovery
equation-discovery.definition: Learning the parameters or terms of a differential equation by fitting it to measured time derivatives of a field.

data-pipeline.title: The Data Science Hierarchy of Needs
data-pipeline.name: Data pipeline
data-pipeline.definition: The infrastructure that collects, stores, moves, cleans and labels data before any model is trained on it.

nyquist-frequency.title: From a Wave to a Picture
nyquist-frequency.name: Nyquist frequency
nyquist-frequency.definition: Half the sampling rate, the highest frequency a sampled signal can represent.

generative-adversarial-network.title: Generative Adversarial Networks (2014)
generative-adversarial-network.name: Generative adversarial network
generative-adversarial-network.definition: A generator network trained against a discriminator network until the generator produces samples the discriminator cannot tell from real data.

combinatorial-explosion.title: Solving Puzzles: How Big Is the Search?
combinatorial-explosion.name: Combinatorial explosion
combinatorial-explosion.definition: The rapid growth in the number of possible states or configurations, which makes exhaustive search impossible and forces learning structure instead.

correlation-matrix.title: Correlation Matrix (Multiple Variables)
correlation-matrix.name: Correlation matrix
correlation-matrix.definition: The matrix of correlation coefficients between every pair of variables, with ones on the diagonal.

simpsons-paradox.title: Correlation Matrix (Multiple Variables)
simpsons-paradox.name: Simpson's paradox
simpsons-paradox.definition: A trend that appears in pooled data reverses or disappears inside every subgroup, because a hidden grouping variable drives it.

box-plot.title: Box and Whisker Plot
box-plot.name: Box plot
box-plot.definition: A summary of a distribution by five numbers: minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum.

first-principles-model.title: Recap: From Empirical Laws to Models
first-principles-model.name: First-principles model
first-principles-model.definition: A model derived from fundamental laws such as conservation and Newton's laws, rather than fitted to a chosen functional form.

inductive-bias.title: Inductive Bias #1: Space and Time
inductive-bias.name: Inductive bias
inductive-bias.definition: The assumptions built into a model or learning method that let it generalise beyond the data it was trained on.

field.title: Inductive Bias #1: Space and Time
field.name: Field
field.definition: A quantity defined at every point in space and time, written u(x, t), such as temperature or velocity.

physical-units.title: Coordinate Systems and Units
physical-units.name: Physical units
physical-units.definition: The dimensions attached to a quantity, such as meters or seconds, which carry its physical meaning and scale.

finite-difference.title: From Discrete to Continuous
finite-difference.name: Finite difference
finite-difference.definition: Approximating a derivative by the difference of function values at nearby points divided by their spacing.

differential-equation.title: Newton's Second Law
differential-equation.name: Differential equation
differential-equation.definition: An equation that relates an unknown function to its derivatives, describing how a quantity changes.

analytical-solution.title: Solving the Equation
analytical-solution.name: Analytical solution
analytical-solution.definition: A closed-form formula that solves an equation exactly, obtained by hand rather than by computation.

ordinary-differential-equation.title: Adding Complexity
ordinary-differential-equation.name: Ordinary differential equation
ordinary-differential-equation.definition: A differential equation for a function of a single variable, usually time.

dynamical-system.title: Adding Complexity
dynamical-system.name: Dynamical system
dynamical-system.definition: A system whose state changes over time according to a fixed rule, such as a differential equation.

conservation-law.title: Inductive Bias #2: Conservation Laws
conservation-law.name: Conservation law
conservation-law.definition: A statement that a quantity is neither created nor destroyed, so its accumulation in a region equals flux in minus flux out.

previewed_on.title: Recap: From Empirical Laws to Models

flux.title: Inductive Bias #2: Conservation Laws
flux.name: Flux
flux.definition: The rate at which a quantity flows across a boundary per unit time.

continuity-equation.title: The Continuity Equation
continuity-equation.name: Continuity equation
continuity-equation.definition: The differential form of a conservation law: the time derivative of a density plus the divergence of its flux equals zero.

divergence.title: Higher Dimensions
divergence.name: Divergence
divergence.definition: A measure of the net outflow of a vector field from a point, the sum of the partial derivatives of its components.

linearization.title: The Reality: Nonlinearity
linearization.name: Linearization
linearization.definition: Approximating a nonlinear system by a linear one near an operating point or equilibrium.

navier-stokes-equations.title: Case Study: Navier-Stokes Equations
navier-stokes-equations.name: Navier-Stokes equations
navier-stokes-equations.definition: The partial differential equations for momentum conservation in a viscous fluid, combining Newton's second law with the law of viscosity.

material-derivative.title: The Lagrangian Derivative
material-derivative.name: Material derivative
material-derivative.definition: The rate of change of a quantity following a moving fluid particle, the local change plus the convective change.

turbulence.title: The Nonlinearity Problem
turbulence.name: Turbulence
turbulence.definition: Irregular, multi-scale fluid motion produced by the nonlinear convective term of the Navier-Stokes equations.

partial-differential-equation.title: Building Block PDEs
partial-differential-equation.name: Partial differential equation
partial-differential-equation.definition: An equation relating a function of several variables, such as space and time, to its partial derivatives.

previewed_on.title: The Same Three Pillars, for a Field

advection-equation.title: The Advection Equation
advection-equation.name: Advection equation
advection-equation.definition: A first-order PDE whose solution is the initial profile transported at constant speed without changing shape.

diffusion-equation.title: The Diffusion Equation
diffusion-equation.name: Diffusion equation
diffusion-equation.definition: A PDE in which a quantity changes at a rate proportional to its curvature, so peaks flatten and the profile spreads out.

wave-equation.title: The Wave Equation
wave-equation.name: Wave equation
wave-equation.definition: A second-order PDE whose solutions are disturbances that propagate at a fixed speed in both directions.

advection-diffusion-equation.title: Advection-Diffusion: Combined Effects
advection-diffusion-equation.name: Advection-diffusion equation
advection-diffusion-equation.definition: A PDE combining transport at a speed with spreading by diffusion, as for a pollutant carried down a river.

reaction-diffusion-equation.title: Reaction-Diffusion
reaction-diffusion-equation.name: Reaction-diffusion equation
reaction-diffusion-equation.definition: A diffusion equation with a local, often nonlinear, reaction or growth term added.

pattern-formation.title: Reaction-Diffusion
pattern-formation.name: Pattern formation
pattern-formation.definition: The spontaneous emergence of spatial structures such as spots and stripes from nonlinear local interactions plus diffusion.

damped-oscillator.title: RC and RLC Circuits
damped-oscillator.name: Damped oscillator
damped-oscillator.definition: A second-order system, like an RLC circuit or a spring with friction, that oscillates while its amplitude decays.

inverse-problem.title: Application: Synthesizers
inverse-problem.name: Inverse problem
inverse-problem.definition: Inferring the causes or parameters of a system, such as a circuit, from observations of its output.

dimensional-analysis.title: Don't Forget: Units Matter
dimensional-analysis.name: Dimensional analysis
dimensional-analysis.definition: Using the units of quantities to check equations, derive relationships, and identify which terms dominate at a given scale.

autoregressive-model.title: Differential Equations as Generative Models
autoregressive-model.name: Autoregressive model
autoregressive-model.definition: A model that generates a sequence by feeding each output back in as the next input, as in time stepping or next-word prediction.

initial-value-problem.title: Differential Equations as Generative Models
initial-value-problem.name: Initial value problem
initial-value-problem.definition: A differential equation together with the state at a starting time, from which the future trajectory is determined.

modeling-assumption.title: All Models Make Assumptions
modeling-assumption.name: Modeling assumption
modeling-assumption.definition: A simplification built into a model, such as linear response or a continuous medium, whose violation explains when the model fails.

recursion.title: Computing as Recursive Rule Application
recursion.name: Recursion
recursion.definition: Generating results by applying a rule repeatedly, each output becoming the next input.

recurrence-relation.title: Example: Fibonacci Sequence
recurrence-relation.name: Recurrence relation
recurrence-relation.definition: An equation that defines each term of a sequence from previous terms, like the Fibonacci rule.

cellular-automaton.title: Cellular Automata: Game of Life
cellular-automaton.name: Cellular automaton
cellular-automaton.definition: A grid of cells updated in discrete steps by a local rule that depends only on each cell's neighbours.

emergence.title: Cellular Automata: Game of Life
emergence.name: Emergence
emergence.definition: Complex global behaviour arising from simple local rules, as in the Game of Life.

discretization.title: Discretization
discretization.name: Discretization
discretization.definition: Replacing continuous derivatives with differences on a grid so a differential equation becomes an algebraic update a computer can run.

euler-method.title: Discretization
euler-method.name: Euler method
euler-method.definition: The simplest time-stepping scheme: advance the state by the current derivative times the time step.

time-step.title: The Role of $\Delta t$
time-step.name: Time step
time-step.definition: The interval between successive updates in a numerical simulation, trading accuracy and stability against speed.

lotka-volterra-model.title: The Lotka-Volterra Model
lotka-volterra-model.name: Lotka-Volterra model
lotka-volterra-model.definition: A pair of nonlinear ODEs for predator and prey populations whose interaction produces sustained oscillations.

parameter-estimation.title: Fitting the Model to Data
parameter-estimation.name: Parameter estimation
parameter-estimation.definition: Choosing the constants of a model so its simulated output matches observed data.

pendulum.title: Case Study: The Pendulum
pendulum.name: Pendulum
pendulum.definition: A mass on a rod whose angle obeys a nonlinear second-order ODE, harmonic only for small swings.

phase-space.title: Pendulum Phase Space
phase-space.name: Phase space
phase-space.definition: The space of all states of a dynamical system, such as angle and angular velocity, in which a trajectory is a curve.

truncation-error.title: Error Analysis: How Accurate?
truncation-error.name: Truncation error
truncation-error.definition: The error a numerical scheme makes by dropping the higher-order terms of a Taylor expansion.

taylor-expansion.title: Error Analysis: How Accurate?
taylor-expansion.name: Taylor expansion
taylor-expansion.definition: Writing a function near a point as a polynomial built from its derivatives at that point.

order-of-accuracy.title: Finite Difference Schemes
order-of-accuracy.name: Order of accuracy
order-of-accuracy.definition: How fast a scheme's error shrinks as the step size shrinks, for example proportional to the step or to its square.

computational-grid.title: Discretizing Space and Time
computational-grid.name: Computational grid
computational-grid.definition: The set of discrete points in space and time at which a numerical solution is computed.

stencil.title: PDE Discretization: Step by Step
stencil.name: Stencil
stencil.definition: The pattern of neighbouring grid points a finite-difference update uses to compute a new value.

explicit-vs-implicit-scheme.title: The Stencil
explicit-vs-implicit-scheme.name: Explicit and implicit schemes
explicit-vs-implicit-scheme.definition: Explicit schemes compute the next state directly from the current one; implicit schemes solve a linear system and are more stable.

crank-nicolson.title: The Stencil
crank-nicolson.name: Crank-Nicolson method
crank-nicolson.definition: An implicit scheme that averages forward and backward time steps, second-order accurate in time and space.

numerical-stability.title: Stability: The CFL Condition
numerical-stability.name: Numerical stability
numerical-stability.definition: Whether errors in a numerical scheme stay bounded or blow up as the computation proceeds.

cfl-condition.title: Stability: The CFL Condition
cfl-condition.name: CFL condition
cfl-condition.definition: The Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy limit on the time step relative to the grid spacing, beyond which an explicit scheme becomes unstable.

runge-kutta.title: Better Integrators: Runge-Kutta
runge-kutta.name: Runge-Kutta method
runge-kutta.definition: A family of time-stepping schemes that sample the slope at several points within a step; RK4 is fourth-order accurate.

adaptive-time-stepping.title: Why RK4?
adaptive-time-stepping.name: Adaptive time stepping
adaptive-time-stepping.definition: Automatically adjusting the time step during a simulation based on an estimate of the local error.

finite-volume-method.title: Finite Volume: The Flux Picture
finite-volume-method.name: Finite volume method
finite-volume-method.definition: A discretization that tracks fluxes between cells so that conserved quantities are preserved exactly.

upwind-scheme.title: Finite Volume: The Flux Picture
upwind-scheme.name: Upwind scheme
upwind-scheme.definition: A discretization that takes flux values from the side the flow is coming from, so information travels in the right direction.

operator-splitting.title: The Discretized Equations
operator-splitting.name: Operator splitting
operator-splitting.definition: Solving a complicated equation by applying its parts, such as diffusion and advection, one after another in each time step.

semi-lagrangian-advection.title: The Discretized Equations
semi-lagrangian-advection.name: Semi-Lagrangian advection
semi-lagrangian-advection.definition: Advecting a quantity by tracing each grid point backward along the velocity to find where its value came from.

pressure-projection.title: Enforcing Incompressibility
pressure-projection.name: Pressure projection
pressure-projection.definition: Making a velocity field divergence-free by solving a Poisson equation for pressure and subtracting its gradient.

rayleigh-benard-convection.title: Rayleigh-Bénard Convection
rayleigh-benard-convection.name: Rayleigh-Benard convection
rayleigh-benard-convection.definition: Convection in a fluid heated from below and cooled from above, which forms rolling cells and drives weather.

model-reduction.title: From 7 Equations to 3: The Saltzman-Lorenz Story
model-reduction.name: Model reduction
model-reduction.definition: Replacing a large model with a smaller one that keeps only the variables that drive the dynamics.

lorenz-system.title: The Lorenz Equations
lorenz-system.name: Lorenz system
lorenz-system.definition: Three coupled nonlinear ODEs reduced from a convection model, the classic example of deterministic chaos.

previewed_on.title: From 7 Equations to 3: The Saltzman-Lorenz Story

strange-attractor.title: The Lorenz Attractor
strange-attractor.name: Strange attractor
strange-attractor.definition: A fractal set in phase space that chaotic trajectories approach and wander on without ever repeating.

sensitivity-to-initial-conditions.title: Sensitivity to Initial Conditions
sensitivity-to-initial-conditions.name: Sensitivity to initial conditions
sensitivity-to-initial-conditions.definition: The property that arbitrarily small differences in starting state grow until trajectories diverge completely.

chaos.title: The Butterfly Effect
chaos.name: Chaos
chaos.definition: Deterministic dynamics in which tiny differences in initial conditions grow exponentially, making long-term prediction impossible.

complex-system.title: What is a Complex System?
complex-system.name: Complex system
complex-system.definition: A system of many interacting parts whose collective behavior cannot be understood by studying the parts one at a time.

ensemble.title: Ensemble of Initial Conditions
ensemble.name: Ensemble
ensemble.definition: A collection of simulations started from slightly different initial conditions, used to represent uncertainty as a distribution.

probability-mass-function.title: From Trajectories to Distribution
probability-mass-function.name: Probability mass function
probability-mass-function.definition: A function giving the probability that a discrete random variable takes each of its possible values.

kernel-density-estimation.title: Estimating PDF from Samples
kernel-density-estimation.name: Kernel density estimation
kernel-density-estimation.definition: Estimating a probability density by placing a small smooth bump on each sample and summing them.

random-variable.title: Random Variables
random-variable.name: Random variable
random-variable.definition: A function that assigns a number to each outcome of a random experiment.

expectation.title: Mean and Variance
expectation.name: Expectation
expectation.definition: The probability-weighted average value of a random variable, its center of mass.

variance.title: Mean and Variance
variance.name: Variance
variance.definition: The expected squared distance of a random variable from its mean, a measure of spread.

joint-probability.title: Joint & Conditional Probability
joint-probability.name: Joint probability
joint-probability.definition: The probability that two or more events or random variables take given values at the same time.

conditional-probability.title: Joint & Conditional Probability
conditional-probability.name: Conditional probability
conditional-probability.definition: The probability of one event given that another event is known to have happened.

independence.title: Independence
independence.name: Independence
independence.definition: Two random variables are independent when knowing one tells you nothing about the other, so their joint probability factorizes.

central-limit-theorem.title: Central Limit Theorem
central-limit-theorem.name: Central limit theorem
central-limit-theorem.definition: The average of many independent random variables with finite variance tends toward a Gaussian distribution.

brownian-motion.title: Brownian Motion
brownian-motion.name: Brownian motion
brownian-motion.definition: The erratic movement of a small particle pushed by random molecular collisions, the physical model of continuous random motion.

random-walk.title: Random Walk
random-walk.name: Random walk
random-walk.definition: A process that moves by a random step at each time, the discrete model of diffusion.

master-equation.title: The Master Equation
master-equation.name: Master equation
master-equation.definition: An equation for how the probability of each state changes in time from the rates of jumping between states.

continuum-limit.title: Taking the Continuum Limit
continuum-limit.name: Continuum limit
continuum-limit.definition: Letting grid spacing and time step shrink to zero so a discrete update rule becomes a differential equation.

stochastic-differential-equation.title: What if $\Delta x \to 0$? Random $dx$ at every $dt$?
stochastic-differential-equation.name: Stochastic differential equation
stochastic-differential-equation.definition: A differential equation with a random forcing term, describing individual noisy trajectories.

coarse-graining.title: From Randomness to Determinism
coarse-graining.name: Coarse-graining
coarse-graining.definition: Describing a system at a larger scale by averaging over fine details, which can turn random microscopic behavior into predictable macroscopic laws.

network.title: Complex Systems on Networks
network.name: Network
network.definition: A set of nodes connected by edges, used to represent systems whose parts interact along specific links.

fitzhugh-nagumo-model.title: How About Neurons to Brains?
fitzhugh-nagumo-model.name: FitzHugh-Nagumo model
fitzhugh-nagumo-model.definition: A two-variable simplification of neuron dynamics that produces spiking and oscillation.

coupled-oscillators.title: Coupled Neurons
coupled-oscillators.name: Coupled oscillators
coupled-oscillators.definition: Several oscillating units that influence each other through connections such as springs or synapses.

synchronization.title: Synchronization
synchronization.name: Synchronization
synchronization.definition: The tendency of coupled oscillators to lock into a common rhythm when coupling is strong enough.

stationarity.title: First Rule: LOOK at the Data
stationarity.name: Stationarity
stationarity.definition: The property that a time series' statistics such as mean and variance do not change over time.

fourier-series.title: Fourier = Linear Model
fourier-series.name: Fourier series
fourier-series.definition: Representing a signal as a weighted sum of sines and cosines at different frequencies.

seasonality.title: What Is Left Is the Weather
seasonality.name: Seasonality
seasonality.definition: A repeating pattern in a time series tied to a calendar period such as a year or a day.

short-time-fourier-transform.title: How the STFT Works
short-time-fourier-transform.name: Short-time Fourier transform
short-time-fourier-transform.definition: Computing the Fourier transform over a sliding window to see how frequency content changes over time.

basis-function.title: General Modal Decomposition
basis-function.name: Basis function
basis-function.definition: One member of a chosen set of functions, such as sines, polynomials or wavelets, whose weighted sum represents a signal.

separation-of-variables.title: Physics of Harmonics
separation-of-variables.name: Separation of variables
separation-of-variables.definition: Solving a partial differential equation by assuming the solution is a product of functions of each variable separately.

normal-mode.title: Standing Waves on a String
normal-mode.name: Normal mode
normal-mode.definition: A pattern of motion in which all parts of a linear system oscillate at the same single frequency.

fermi-pasta-ulam-tsingou-problem.title: FPUT: Energy Recurrence
fermi-pasta-ulam-tsingou-problem.name: Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou problem
fermi-pasta-ulam-tsingou-problem.definition: A 1953 simulation of a nonlinear spring chain in which energy unexpectedly returned to its initial mode instead of spreading out.

arima.title: ARIMA and Extensions
arima.name: ARIMA
arima.definition: An extension of autoregressive models that adds differencing to remove trends and moving-average terms on past errors.

nonlinear-autoregressive-model.title: Nonlinear AR Extensions
nonlinear-autoregressive-model.name: Nonlinear autoregressive model
nonlinear-autoregressive-model.definition: An autoregressive model whose features include nonlinear functions of past values, such as their squares and products.

logistic-map.title: The Logistic Map
logistic-map.name: Logistic map
logistic-map.definition: The discrete population model x next equals r x (1 minus x), which shows period doubling and chaos as r grows.

system-identification.title: Given Data, Find the Map
system-identification.name: System identification
system-identification.definition: Estimating the parameters of a dynamical model from measured input and output data.

numerical-differentiation.title: Learning $\dot{u} = f(u)$
numerical-differentiation.name: Numerical differentiation
numerical-differentiation.definition: Estimating derivatives from sampled data, a step that amplifies noise.

feature-library.title: The Library Idea
feature-library.name: Feature library
feature-library.definition: A set of candidate functions of the state from which a sparse model selects the terms of an equation.

dimensionality-reduction.title: Why Reduce Dimensions?
dimensionality-reduction.name: Dimensionality reduction
dimensionality-reduction.definition: Representing high-dimensional data with fewer variables while keeping most of its structure.

curse-of-dimensionality.title: Why Reduce Dimensions?
curse-of-dimensionality.name: Curse of dimensionality
curse-of-dimensionality.definition: As the number of dimensions grows, data becomes sparse and models need exponentially more samples.

principal-component-analysis.title: Principal Components
principal-component-analysis.name: Principal component analysis
principal-component-analysis.definition: Finding orthogonal directions of maximum variance in data and projecting onto the top few.

standardization.title: Center and Standardize
standardization.name: Standardization
standardization.definition: Rescaling each feature to zero mean and unit standard deviation so features are comparable.

reconstruction-error.title: Reconstruction Error
reconstruction-error.name: Reconstruction error
reconstruction-error.definition: The distance between original data and its approximation after projecting to fewer dimensions and back.

lagrange-multiplier.title: Lagrange Multipliers
lagrange-multiplier.name: Lagrange multiplier
lagrange-multiplier.definition: A variable added to turn a constrained optimization problem into an unconstrained one.

explained-variance.title: Eigenvalues Tell the Story
explained-variance.name: Explained variance
explained-variance.definition: The fraction of total variance in the data captured by a given set of principal components.

singular-value-decomposition.title: SVD: Singular Value Decomposition
singular-value-decomposition.name: Singular value decomposition
singular-value-decomposition.definition: Factoring any matrix as U times Sigma times V transpose, with orthogonal U and V and nonnegative singular values.

low-rank-approximation.title: Low-Rank Approximation
low-rank-approximation.name: Low-rank approximation
low-rank-approximation.definition: Approximating a matrix by keeping only its largest singular values and their vectors.

eigenfaces.title: Eigenfaces: Faces as Points in High-D Space
eigenfaces.name: Eigenfaces
eigenfaces.definition: Principal components of a set of face images, used as a basis to represent and reconstruct faces.

scree-plot.title: Scree Plot: How Many Components?
scree-plot.name: Scree plot
scree-plot.definition: A plot of singular values or eigenvalues in decreasing order used to choose how many components to keep.

linear-dynamical-system.title: When Is a System Linear?
linear-dynamical-system.name: Linear dynamical system
linear-dynamical-system.definition: A system whose rate of change is a constant matrix times its state.

eigendecomposition.title: Eigendecomposition of $A$
eigendecomposition.name: Eigendecomposition
eigendecomposition.definition: Writing a square matrix as V Lambda V inverse, with eigenvectors in V and eigenvalues on the diagonal of Lambda.

modal-decoupling.title: The Decoupling Trick
modal-decoupling.name: Modal decoupling
modal-decoupling.definition: Changing to eigenvector coordinates so a coupled linear system becomes independent one-dimensional equations.

linear-stability.title: What Do Eigenvalues Tell Us?
linear-stability.name: Linear stability
linear-stability.definition: How eigenvalues of a linear system determine whether solutions grow, decay or oscillate.

vortex-shedding.title: Flow Past a Cylinder
vortex-shedding.name: Vortex shedding
vortex-shedding.definition: The periodic release of alternating vortices behind an obstacle in a flow.

snapshot-matrix.title: The Snapshot Matrix & Its SVD
snapshot-matrix.name: Snapshot matrix
snapshot-matrix.definition: A data matrix whose columns are the system's full state measured at successive times.

proper-orthogonal-decomposition.title: SVD Modes of the Flow
proper-orthogonal-decomposition.name: Proper orthogonal decomposition
proper-orthogonal-decomposition.definition: Applying SVD to a snapshot matrix to get energy-ranked spatial modes of a field.

pseudo-inverse.title: Solving for $A$
pseudo-inverse.name: Pseudo-inverse
pseudo-inverse.definition: A generalized inverse of a rectangular matrix that gives the least-squares solution of a linear system.

dynamic-mode-decomposition.title: DMD: Steps 1–2
dynamic-mode-decomposition.name: Dynamic mode decomposition
dynamic-mode-decomposition.definition: Fitting a best linear map between successive snapshots and decomposing it into spatial modes each with one growth rate and frequency.

previewed_on.title: From Time Series to a Dynamical Model

koopman-operator.title: Beyond Dynamic Mode Decomposition
koopman-operator.name: Koopman operator
koopman-operator.definition: A linear operator that advances functions of the state of a nonlinear system, making nonlinear dynamics linear in a larger space.

savitzky-golay-filter.title: Differentiation Methods
savitzky-golay-filter.name: Savitzky-Golay filter
savitzky-golay-filter.definition: Smoothing and differentiating data by fitting a low-degree polynomial in a sliding window.

sparse-regression.title: Approaches to Sparsity
sparse-regression.name: Sparse regression
sparse-regression.definition: Regression that forces most coefficients to be exactly zero so only a few terms remain.

sequential-thresholded-least-squares.title: Approaches to Sparsity
sequential-thresholded-least-squares.name: Sequential thresholded least squares
sequential-thresholded-least-squares.definition: Repeatedly solving least squares and zeroing coefficients below a threshold until the active set stops changing.

sindy.title: SINDy in Python
sindy.name: SINDy
sindy.definition: Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics: discovering a governing equation by sparse regression over a library of candidate terms.

pde-discovery.title: Building the PDE Feature Matrix
pde-discovery.name: PDE discovery
pde-discovery.definition: Extending sparse regression to libraries of spatial derivatives to learn partial differential equations from data on a grid.

self-organization.title: Why Does Deep Learning Work?
self-organization.name: Self-Organization
self-organization.definition: Global order or capability emerging from many simple elements that adapt and coordinate locally, without a central designer.

rule-based-system.title: Rules vs. the Ability to Learn
rule-based-system.name: Rule-Based System
rule-based-system.definition: A program that acts by following explicit rules written by experts, rather than learning its behaviour from data.

voltage-clamp.title: From Theory to Biology: The Squid Giant Axon
voltage-clamp.name: Voltage Clamp
voltage-clamp.definition: An experimental technique that holds a neuron's membrane voltage fixed so the ionic currents through it can be measured.

hodgkin-huxley-model.title: The Hodgkin-Huxley Model
hodgkin-huxley-model.name: Hodgkin-Huxley Model
hodgkin-huxley-model.definition: A set of coupled differential equations, fitted to squid axon data, that describes how ion channels produce a neuron's spike.

previewed_on.title: From Theory to Biology: The Squid Giant Axon

representation-learning.title: Why Depth? Hierarchical Feature Learning
representation-learning.name: Representation Learning
representation-learning.definition: Letting a model learn its own features from raw data, with deeper layers building more abstract features from simpler ones.

adam-optimizer.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent and Variants
adam-optimizer.name: Adam Optimizer
adam-optimizer.definition: A gradient-based optimizer that adapts the step size of each parameter using running averages of its gradients and squared gradients.

pytorch.title: Training in Practice: PyTorch
pytorch.name: PyTorch
pytorch.definition: A Python library for building and training neural networks, with tensors, layers, optimizers and automatic differentiation.

dropout.title: Overfitting and Regularization
dropout.name: Dropout
dropout.definition: A regularization technique that randomly switches off neurons during training so the network cannot rely on any single unit.

early-stopping.title: Overfitting and Regularization
early-stopping.name: Early Stopping
early-stopping.definition: Halting training when the validation loss stops improving, to avoid overfitting the training data.

ising-model.title: The Ising Model (Lenz 1920, Ising 1925)
ising-model.name: Ising Model
ising-model.definition: A statistical mechanics model of a grid of up-or-down spins whose neighbours prefer to align, used to study magnetism and phase transitions.

metropolis-hastings.title: Ising Model: The Algorithm
metropolis-hastings.name: Metropolis-Hastings Algorithm
metropolis-hastings.definition: A sampling method that proposes random changes and accepts them with a probability set by the change in energy or likelihood.

hopfield-network.title: From Spins to Neurons: Hopfield Networks (1982)
hopfield-network.name: Hopfield Network
hopfield-network.definition: A fully connected network of binary neurons with symmetric weights whose energy minima store patterns as memories.

energy-based-model.title: From Spins to Neurons: Hopfield Networks (1982)
energy-based-model.name: Energy-Based Model
energy-based-model.definition: A model that assigns an energy to every configuration so that likely or desired configurations have low energy.

associative-memory.title: How Hopfield Networks Work
associative-memory.name: Associative Memory
associative-memory.definition: A memory that retrieves a complete stored pattern from a partial or corrupted version of it.

attention.name: Attention
attention.definition: A mechanism that combines stored values weighted by the softmax similarity between a query and a set of keys.

boltzmann-machine.title: Boltzmann Machines: Adding Stochasticity (Optional)
boltzmann-machine.name: Boltzmann Machine
boltzmann-machine.definition: A stochastic network of visible and hidden binary units whose joint probability follows a Boltzmann distribution over an energy function.

boltzmann-distribution.title: Boltzmann Machines: The Math
boltzmann-distribution.name: Boltzmann Distribution
boltzmann-distribution.definition: A probability distribution in which a configuration's probability decays exponentially with its energy divided by temperature.

hidden-state.title: The RNN Architecture
hidden-state.name: Hidden State
hidden-state.definition: An internal vector a sequence model updates at each time step to carry information about the past.

state-space-model.title: RNN as a State-Space Model
state-space-model.name: State-Space Model
state-space-model.definition: A model in which a hidden state evolves by an update rule driven by inputs, and observations are read out from that state.

backpropagation-through-time.title: Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT)
backpropagation-through-time.name: Backpropagation Through Time
backpropagation-through-time.definition: Training a recurrent network by unrolling it over the sequence and applying backpropagation through every time step.

vanishing-gradient.title: Vanishing Gradients: Interactive
vanishing-gradient.name: Vanishing Gradient
vanishing-gradient.definition: The shrinking of gradients as they are multiplied back through many layers or time steps, which stops early parts of a network from learning.

spectral-radius.title: Vanishing Gradients: Interactive
spectral-radius.name: Spectral Radius
spectral-radius.definition: The largest absolute value among a matrix's eigenvalues, which sets whether repeated multiplication by it grows or shrinks vectors.

lstm.title: LSTM: Solving the Vanishing Gradient
lstm.name: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
lstm.definition: A recurrent network whose gates control what a cell state forgets, stores and outputs, letting it keep information over long sequences.

reservoir-computing.title: Echo State Networks (Jaeger, 2001)
reservoir-computing.name: Reservoir Computing
reservoir-computing.definition: Using a fixed, randomly connected recurrent network as a dynamical reservoir and training only a linear readout from its states.

echo-state-property.title: The Echo State Property
echo-state-property.name: Echo State Property
echo-state-property.definition: The requirement that a reservoir's state depends on its input history and forgets its initial condition over time.

physical-reservoir-computing.title: Physical Reservoir Computing
physical-reservoir-computing.name: Physical Reservoir Computing
physical-reservoir-computing.definition: Using a real physical system with nonlinear, fading-memory dynamics, such as optics or mechanics, as the reservoir of a reservoir computer.

kuramoto-sivashinsky-equation.title: The Kuramoto-Sivashinsky Equation
kuramoto-sivashinsky-equation.name: Kuramoto-Sivashinsky Equation
kuramoto-sivashinsky-equation.definition: A fourth-order nonlinear PDE from flame fronts and chemical oscillations that is a standard test case for spatiotemporal chaos.

spatiotemporal-chaos.title: The Kuramoto-Sivashinsky Equation
spatiotemporal-chaos.name: Spatiotemporal Chaos
spatiotemporal-chaos.definition: Chaotic behaviour that is irregular in both space and time, with sensitive dependence on initial conditions.

lyapunov-time.title: Pathak et al.: Architecture & Results
lyapunov-time.name: Lyapunov Time
lyapunov-time.definition: The characteristic time over which small errors in a chaotic system grow by a factor of e, setting the horizon of useful prediction.

symbolic-regression.title: What is Symbolic Regression?
symbolic-regression.name: Symbolic regression
symbolic-regression.definition: Searching over mathematical expressions to find a formula that fits data, without fixing the candidate terms in advance.

expression-tree.title: Expressions as Trees
expression-tree.name: Expression Tree
expression-tree.definition: A tree representation of a formula in which internal nodes are operators and leaves are variables or constants.

genetic-programming.title: The Genetic Algorithm
genetic-programming.name: Genetic Programming
genetic-programming.definition: An evolutionary search that improves a population of programs or expression trees through selection, crossover and mutation.

fitness-function.title: The Genetic Algorithm
fitness-function.name: Fitness Function
fitness-function.definition: The score an evolutionary algorithm uses to rank candidates, often fit error plus a penalty for complexity.

selection.title: Selection
selection.name: Selection
selection.definition: The step of an evolutionary algorithm that chooses which candidates reproduce, favouring those with better fitness.
