crossover.title: Crossover: Swapping Subtrees
crossover.name: Crossover
crossover.definition: Creating offspring in an evolutionary algorithm by combining parts of two parents, such as swapping subtrees.

mutation.title: Mutation: Random Changes
mutation.name: Mutation
mutation.definition: A random change to a candidate in an evolutionary algorithm, which introduces new material into the population.

keplers-third-law.title: Now Do It On Something Real
keplers-third-law.name: Kepler's Third Law
keplers-third-law.definition: The law that a planet's orbital period squared is proportional to its orbital distance cubed, divided by the star's mass.

power-law.title: A Straight Line Where You Did Not Expect One
power-law.name: Power Law
power-law.definition: A relationship of the form y = C x^a, which appears as a straight line on a log-log plot.

pareto-front.title: The Accuracy-Complexity Tradeoff
pareto-front.name: Pareto Front
pareto-front.definition: The set of candidates that no other candidate beats on every objective at once, such as accuracy and simplicity.

pysr.title: PySR: Modern Symbolic Regression
pysr.name: PySR
pysr.definition: A high-performance open-source library for symbolic regression using parallel evolving populations.

bloat.title: Challenges and Solutions
bloat.name: Bloat
bloat.definition: The tendency of evolved expression trees to grow larger without improving their fitness.

boundary-condition.title: The Problem We Want to Solve
boundary-condition.name: Boundary Condition
boundary-condition.definition: A constraint on a differential equation's solution at the edges of its domain or at the initial time.

basis-expansion.title: The Classical Approach: Basis Functions
basis-expansion.name: Basis Expansion
basis-expansion.definition: Writing an unknown function as a weighted sum of fixed known functions such as sines or polynomials.

pde-residual.title: Defining the Residual
pde-residual.name: PDE Residual
pde-residual.definition: What remains when a candidate solution is substituted into a differential equation; it is zero everywhere for an exact solution.

collocation-method.title: Collocation Methods
collocation-method.name: Collocation Method
collocation-method.definition: Finding an approximate solution of a differential equation by making its residual small at a chosen set of points.

physics-informed-neural-network.title: The PINN: Neural Network as Solution
physics-informed-neural-network.name: Physics-informed neural network
physics-informed-neural-network.definition: A neural network trained so that its output satisfies a differential equation, by adding the equation residual to the loss.

previewed_on.title: Where We Are in the Course

automatic-differentiation.title: Automatic Differentiation
automatic-differentiation.name: Automatic Differentiation
automatic-differentiation.definition: Computing exact derivatives of a program by applying the chain rule through its computation graph.

physics-informed-loss.title: The PINN Loss Function
physics-informed-loss.name: Physics-Informed Loss
physics-informed-loss.definition: A loss that adds weighted terms for data fit, PDE residual and boundary conditions so one optimisation respects both data and physics.

mesh-free-method.title: PINN vs Classical Methods
mesh-free-method.name: Mesh-Free Method
mesh-free-method.definition: A numerical method that evaluates the solution at scattered points without building a mesh or grid.

forward-problem.title: Forward Problem: Solving a Known PDE
forward-problem.name: Forward Problem
forward-problem.definition: Computing a system's solution when the governing equation and all its parameters are known.

loss-balancing.title: Why PINNs Can Fail
loss-balancing.name: Loss Balancing
loss-balancing.definition: Choosing or adapting the weights of different loss terms so that none dominates training.

spectral-bias.title: Spectral Bias in Action
spectral-bias.name: Spectral Bias
spectral-bias.definition: The tendency of neural networks to learn low-frequency components of a function before high-frequency ones.

fourier-features.title: Fourier Feature Networks
fourier-features.name: Fourier Features
fourier-features.definition: Mapping inputs through sines and cosines of random frequencies before a network so it can represent high-frequency detail.

operator.title: What Is an Operator?
operator.name: Operator
operator.definition: A map that takes a function as input and returns another function.

discretization-invariance.title: Why Functions, Not Vectors?
discretization-invariance.name: Discretization Invariance
discretization-invariance.definition: The property that a learned model works on input and output grids of any resolution without retraining.

operator-universal-approximation.title: Universal Approximation for Operators
operator-universal-approximation.name: Universal Approximation for Operators
operator-universal-approximation.definition: The theorem that a suitable neural network can approximate any continuous nonlinear operator between function spaces.

neural-operator.title: The Operator Learning Setup
neural-operator.name: Neural Operator
neural-operator.definition: A neural network that maps whole input functions to output functions, such as initial conditions to PDE solutions.

solution-operator.title: The Operator Learning Setup
solution-operator.name: Solution Operator
solution-operator.definition: The map that takes a PDE's input data, such as an initial condition or forcing, to its solution.

modal-decomposition.title: Spatial-Temporal Modal Decomposition
modal-decomposition.name: Modal Decomposition
modal-decomposition.definition: Writing a field as a sum of spatial modes weighted by time-dependent coefficients.

deeponet.title: DeepONet Architecture
deeponet.name: DeepONet
deeponet.definition: A neural operator that combines a branch network encoding the input function with a trunk network encoding the query point by a dot product.

greens-function.title: Green's Functions: The Integral Solution
greens-function.name: Green's Function
greens-function.definition: The response of a linear differential equation to a point impulse, from which any solution is built by integrating against the forcing.

integral-kernel-layer.title: From Green's Functions to Neural Operator Layers
integral-kernel-layer.name: Integral Kernel Layer
integral-kernel-layer.definition: A neural network layer that transforms a function by integrating it against a learned kernel, generalising a weight matrix to functions.

fourier-neural-operator.title: FNO Layer: Interactive
fourier-neural-operator.name: Fourier Neural Operator
fourier-neural-operator.definition: A neural operator whose layers multiply learned weights on a truncated set of Fourier modes, acting as a learned global convolution.

self-supervised-learning.title: Self-Supervised Learning
self-supervised-learning.name: Self-Supervised Learning
self-supervised-learning.definition: Learning from unlabeled data by predicting part of the data from other parts, so the data supplies its own labels.

next-token-prediction.title: Self-Supervised Learning
next-token-prediction.name: Next-Token Prediction
next-token-prediction.definition: The training objective of predicting each token in a sequence from the tokens before it.

pretraining.title: Pre-training at Scale
pretraining.name: Pretraining
pretraining.definition: The first, large-scale training stage of a model on broad unlabeled data before it is adapted to specific tasks.

foundation-model.title: Pre-training at Scale
foundation-model.name: Foundation Model
foundation-model.definition: A large model pretrained on broad data that can be adapted to many downstream tasks.

transformer.title: The Transformer
transformer.name: Transformer
transformer.definition: A neural network architecture built from stacked attention layers that processes a whole sequence at once rather than step by step.

scaling-law.title: Scaling Laws
scaling-law.name: Scaling Law
scaling-law.definition: An empirical power-law relation showing how model loss falls as compute, data, or parameters grow.

fine-tuning.title: Adaptation: From Raw Model to Useful Assistant
fine-tuning.name: Fine-Tuning
fine-tuning.definition: Continuing to train a pretrained model on a smaller, task-specific dataset to adapt its behavior.

rlhf.title: Adaptation: From Raw Model to Useful Assistant
rlhf.name: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
rlhf.definition: Adapting a language model with a reward model learned from human preference judgments.

in-context-learning.title: Adaptation: From Raw Model to Useful Assistant
in-context-learning.name: In-Context Learning
in-context-learning.definition: A model adapting to a task from examples given in its prompt, without any weight updates.

emergent-capability.title: Emergent Capabilities
emergent-capability.name: Emergent Capability
emergent-capability.definition: An ability that appears in large models but seems absent in smaller ones, sometimes argued to be a measurement artifact.

protein-structure-prediction.title: AlphaFold: Protein Structure Solved
protein-structure-prediction.name: Protein Structure Prediction
protein-structure-prediction.definition: Predicting the 3D folded shape of a protein from its amino acid sequence, as done by AlphaFold.

protein-language-model.title: ESM-3: Generating New Proteins
protein-language-model.name: Protein Language Model
protein-language-model.definition: A language model trained on protein sequences, treating amino acids as tokens, used to predict or design proteins.

ai-weather-forecasting.title: AI Weather Forecasting
ai-weather-forecasting.name: AI Weather Forecasting
ai-weather-forecasting.definition: Learned models such as GraphCast and GenCast that predict global weather from reanalysis data, rivaling numerical forecasts.

evolutionary-search.title: FunSearch: Provable Mathematical Discovery
evolutionary-search.name: Evolutionary Search
evolutionary-search.definition: An optimization loop that proposes candidates, scores them with an evaluator, and keeps and mutates the best ones.

ai-agent.title: Agent = LLM + Tools + Memory + Planning
ai-agent.name: AI Agent
ai-agent.definition: A system in which a language model plans, chooses tools, executes actions, and iterates toward a goal using memory.

tool-use.title: Agent = LLM + Tools + Memory + Planning
tool-use.name: Tool Use
tool-use.definition: A language model calling external functions such as code, search, or simulators through structured descriptions of their inputs.

react-loop.title: Code: The Agent Loop
react-loop.name: ReAct Loop
react-loop.definition: An agent loop that interleaves reasoning steps with actions and observations until a task is done.

coding-agent.title: Inside a Real Agent: Claude Code
coding-agent.name: Coding Agent
coding-agent.definition: An AI agent whose tools read, edit, search, and run code in a software project.

prompt-engineering.title: Prompt Engineering = System Design
prompt-engineering.name: Prompt Engineering
prompt-engineering.definition: Designing the instructions, tools, and constraints given to a language model to shape its behavior.

science-agent.title: Coding Agent → Science Agent
science-agent.name: Science Agent
science-agent.definition: An AI agent whose tools are scientific operations such as data analysis, simulation, literature search, and lab experiments.

autonomous-discovery.title: Timeline of Autonomous Discovery
autonomous-discovery.name: Autonomous Discovery
autonomous-discovery.definition: Scientific discovery in which AI systems generate hypotheses, design and run experiments, and analyze results with little human input.

multi-agent-system.title: Robin: Multi-Agent Drug Discovery
multi-agent-system.name: Multi-Agent System
multi-agent-system.definition: A system in which several AI agents with different roles cooperate on a task.

previewed_on.title: Inside a Real Agent: Claude Code

scientific-method.title: The Mapping
scientific-method.name: Scientific Method
scientific-method.definition: The cycle of observing, hypothesizing, experimenting, analyzing, and revising that produces scientific knowledge.

hallucination.title: The Hallucination Problem
hallucination.name: Hallucination
hallucination.definition: A language model producing fluent, confident output that is factually false or fabricated.

mechanistic-interpretability.title: Do LLMs Have "Emotions"?
mechanistic-interpretability.name: Mechanistic Interpretability
mechanistic-interpretability.definition: Studying a trained network's internal representations and circuits to explain how they cause its behavior.

reward-hacking.title: Do LLMs Have "Emotions"?
reward-hacking.name: Reward Hacking
reward-hacking.definition: A model maximizing its training or evaluation signal in unintended ways that defeat the actual goal.

research-taste.title: Automatable vs. Needs Human Judgment
research-taste.name: Research Taste
research-taste.definition: The judgment to recognize which questions matter and which results are meaningful, built through repeated iteration.

engineering-responsibility.title: Means to Ends
engineering-responsibility.name: Engineering Responsibility
engineering-responsibility.definition: An engineer's awareness of where their work sits in a chain of tools and ends, and of the purposes it ultimately serves.

ai-unpredictability.title: AI Makes This Worse
ai-unpredictability.name: AI Unpredictability
ai-unpredictability.definition: The fact that capable AI systems behave and get used in ways their builders cannot fully foresee, traded off against their usefulness.

consequence-distribution.title: The Consequence Tree
consequence-distribution.name: Consequence Distribution
consequence-distribution.definition: Viewing a tool's outcomes as a probability distribution over good and bad effects, to be shifted and narrowed.

ai-safety.title: We Already Manage Dangerous Tools
ai-safety.name: AI Safety
ai-safety.definition: Practices and standards for managing the risks of AI systems, analogous to warning labels and clinical trials for other technologies.

human-centered-testing.title: Human-Centered Testing
human-centered-testing.name: Human-Centered Testing
human-centered-testing.definition: Releasing a tool by prototyping, watching real users, documenting failures, and writing guidance before wide release.

applied-ethics.title: Three Levels of Ethical Thinking
applied-ethics.name: Applied Ethics
applied-ethics.definition: Ethical reasoning about whether a specific action or technology is good or bad.

normative-ethics.title: Normative Ethics: Theories of Good
normative-ethics.name: Normative Ethics
normative-ethics.definition: Theories such as utilitarianism, deontology, and virtue ethics that say what should govern moral judgments.

meta-ethics.title: Meta-Ethics: Does Good Exist?
meta-ethics.name: Meta-Ethics
meta-ethics.definition: The study of whether moral facts exist and what moral claims mean.

epistemic-humility.title: Knowing You Don't Know
epistemic-humility.name: Epistemic Humility
epistemic-humility.definition: Acknowledging that one's knowledge rests on assumptions that can fail and actively inspecting them.

previewed_on.title: Two Principles for Acting Under Uncertainty

bias-to-action.title: Bias to Action
bias-to-action.name: Bias to Action
bias-to-action.definition: Acting on a best current hypothesis and learning from feedback rather than waiting for certainty.

previewed_on.title: Two Principles for Acting Under Uncertainty

problem-formulation.title: Problem Definition as Meta-Skill
problem-formulation.name: Problem Formulation
problem-formulation.definition: Defining what problem to solve and how to frame it, a skill prior to choosing any method.

previewed_on.title: Why the Toolbox Is Not Enough
